qs.q: What is the correct syntax for referring to an external script called "xxx.js"?
qs.e: External JavaScript files have the extension .js. To use one, the name of the file is put in the `src` (source) attribute of a `<script>` tag, e.g. `<script src="myScript.js"></script>`. The reference may be placed in the `<head>` or the `<body>`, and the script behaves as if it were written exactly where the `<script>` tag is. `href` is used by `<a>` and `<link>`, while `name` and `link` are not valid attributes of `<script>`.

qs.q: Why are event handlers needed in JavaScript?

c.x: To change the behaviour of browser windows only
To add innerHTML to the page code
To respond to occurrences (events) such as clicks and page loads

qs.e: HTML events are things that happen to HTML elements, either caused by the browser (the page finished loading) or by the user (a button was clicked, an input field was changed). Event handler attributes such as `onclick` or `onchange` let JavaScript code run when these occurrences are detected, so the page can react to them. Event handlers have nothing to do with changing the server location, and they are not limited to browser windows.

qs.q: Which operator is used to check whether two values are equal and of the same data type?
qs.e: `===` is the strict equality operator: it is true only when both the value and the type are equal. `==` compares only the values, `=` is the assignment operator, and `!==` means not equal in value or not equal in type.

c.x: Searches for "cis" as a case-sensitive match
Searches for "cis" as a case-insensitive match

qs.e: `search()` looks for a value (here a regular expression) in a string and returns the position of the match. The `/i` modifier makes the regular expression case-insensitive, so `/cis/i` matches "CIS" in "Visit CIS!" and `n` becomes 6 (the position of the match). Without `/i` the search would be case-sensitive, would not find "cis" and would return -1.

qs.q: Which is the correct way to write a JavaScript array?
qs.e: An array can be created with the `new Array()` constructor by passing the elements, separated by commas, inside parentheses, as in the lecture example `new Array("Saab", "Volvo", "BMW")`. The other options use invalid syntax: index:value pairs, colons and equal signs are not allowed in the argument list, and `new Array=` is not a constructor call.

qs.q: Which of the following built-in methods is used to remove the last element from an array and return that element?
qs.e: The `pop()` method removes the last element of an array and returns the value that was "popped out". `push()` does the opposite: it adds a new element at the end and returns the new array length. `last()` and `get()` are not array methods.
